title: Dali's Three Pagodas Are ~1,200 Years Old — But the Temple Isn't | China Travel Expert
description:
Everyone photographs the Three Pagodas of Chongsheng Temple in Dali — but here's the part most visitors miss: the pagodas and the temple are not the same age at all.

The tallest pagoda, Qianxun, went up in the 9th century — about 69 metres tall and 16 tiers — with the two slimmer pagodas added a bit later. Earthquakes repeatedly destroyed the temple that once stood here, yet the three towers kept standing. The grand temple complex you walk through today is a modern reconstruction, built around the pagodas in 2005. So the pagodas are the real ~1,200-year-old relics; the halls behind them are brand new.

🧭 Expert Tip: for the honest history, give the new upper halls a quick pass and spend your time at the base of the three pagodas and the reflecting pool — that's the part that's actually ancient.
